title: Unit 10 Quiz · Basics of Government and Citizenship
description: 10 questions about Unit 10. Read each question carefully. Pick the best answer. One question asks you to pick all the answers that are true.

questions.text: What are the three big jobs a government does for a community?
options: Selling toys, making games, and baking bread.
Picking everyone's friends, food, and clothes.
Keeping order, keeping people safe, and caring for the common good.
Collecting taxes and nothing else.
questions.why: A government keeps order (fair rules, like a property line), keeps people safe (like firefighters), and cares for the common good (things that help everyone, like a park).

questions.lesson: 3.10.02 U.S. Constitution and Power from the People
questions.text: The U.S. Constitution starts with the words "We the People." Where does the government's power come from?
options: The President.
The people.
The army.
The king of England.
questions.why: "We the People" means the power comes from the people. The people choose their leaders by voting, and the leaders must follow the Constitution too.

options: A speech a leader gives on the first day of the job.
A list of every law ever passed.
A book of stories about a country's history.
A written plan that sets up a government, gives it its jobs, and sets its limits.
questions.why: A constitution is a written plan for a government. It sets up the government, gives it its jobs, and sets its limits. The U.S. and Florida each have one.

questions.text: The trash on your street needs to be picked up. Which level of government does that job?
options: Local government (your city or county).
State government (Florida).
National government (the whole country).
No level of government.
questions.why: Trash pickup happens right by your front door. Your city or county, the local government, sends the trash truck.

questions.text: Which job belongs to the national government?
options: Giving out Florida driver's licenses.
Making the dollar bills used in every state.
Lending books at your town library.
Picking up the trash on your street.
questions.why: Only the national government makes U.S. money, so one dollar works the same in all 50 states. Driver's licenses are a state job; the library and trash pickup are local.

questions.text: True or false: The Florida Constitution sets up Florida's state government, and the U.S. Constitution sets up the national government.
options: True
False
questions.why: True. Florida has its own constitution for its state government, and the U.S. Constitution sets up the government for the whole country.

questions.text: Why does a voting booth have a curtain?
options: So the line moves faster.
So nobody has to count the votes.
So each voter can choose in private, and no one can watch or push them.
So only important people can vote.
questions.why: The curtain makes a secret ballot: each person votes in private. No one can watch, and no one can push them to pick something.

questions.text: On July 4, Americans celebrate Independence Day. What happened on July 4, 1776?
options: The Constitution was signed.
Leaders approved the Declaration of Independence, saying the 13 colonies were free from Great Britain's king.
The first Veterans Day parade marched down Main Street.
Florida became a state.
questions.why: On July 4, 1776, the Declaration of Independence was adopted. It said the 13 colonies were free from the king. The Constitution came later, in 1787.

questions.text: Which of these are civic virtues? Pick ALL that are true.
options: Civility: treating people with respect, even when you disagree.
Being the loudest person in the room.
Volunteerism: choosing to help your community without being told to.
Responsibility: doing what you said you would do.
questions.why: Civility, volunteerism, and responsibility are civic virtues (so is cooperation). Being the loudest is not: civility means respect, not winning by shouting.

questions.text: In 1955, Rosa Parks calmly refused to give up her bus seat, even though she knew she could be arrested. What did she show?
options: That only Presidents can be heroes.
That she was tired of walking.
That rules never matter.
Heroism: great courage.
questions.why: Rosa Parks showed heroism, great courage. Heroes are not only Presidents: any citizen can show heroism. Her choice helped change unfair bus laws.
